one_line_reason: Multiple independent meta-analyses and a metabolic-syndrome RCT show oral green coffee bean extract modestly lowers blood pressure, lipids, and glucose, but the identity's own integrity_hold flags a retracted GCBE weight-loss trial that likely contaminated earlier pooled weight/BMI literature.

selected.population: adults, mostly overweight (meta-analysis, 15 studies/19 arms, n=637)
selected.intervention: green coffee bean extract, oral, across pooled RCTs
selected.primary_outcome: cardio-metabolic risk factors: total cholesterol, fasting glucose, blood pressure, body weight, BMI
selected.why_selected: broadest and most comprehensive cardio-metabolic meta-analysis in the shortlist, though weight/BMI findings carry the highest risk of being influenced by the retracted GCBE trial.

selected.intervention: green coffee bean extract, oral, across pooled RCTs
selected.dose_as_stated: not stated (dose-response meta-regression performed but abstract gives no single dose)
selected.primary_outcome: systolic/diastolic blood pressure and heart rate
selected.why_selected: most recent (2024), methodologically explicit dose-response meta-analysis focused specifically on blood pressure, an outcome independent of the contested weight-loss literature.

selected.intervention: green coffee extract, oral, across pooled RCTs
selected.dose_as_stated: subgroup effect on insulin significant at doses ≥400 mg/day
selected.why_selected: gives an actual dose threshold (≥400 mg/day) that can be checked against label amounts, for a glycemic outcome distinct from weight.

selected.population: adults with metabolic syndrome (RCT, randomized, dose and duration stated)
selected.intervention: decaffeinated green coffee bean extract capsules, oral, twice daily, 8 weeks
selected.primary_outcome: systolic blood pressure, fasting blood glucose, insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), waist circumference, appetite
selected.why_selected: single, clearly dosed primary RCT (not a pooled meta-analysis) in a clinical population, useful for verifying a label-mappable dose independent of any retracted-trial contamination.

blockers: This identity's own integrity_hold lists two retracted PMIDs (22291473, 25340633) for a well-known fraudulent GCBE weight-loss crossover trial; several of the selected meta-analyses (especially 34981487's weight/BMI findings) were published after that retraction and central verification must confirm the retracted study was excluded from their pooled data before citing any weight-loss claim.

Effective doses and preparations vary widely across pooled studies (roughly 50-1200 mg/day, caffeinated vs. decaffeinated, %chlorogenic-acid standardization unspecified), so a single label dose cannot be assumed from the meta-analyses alone.
One selected trial (29307310) is in a metabolic-syndrome clinical population rather than general healthy supplement users.

excluded_pmids.reason: Meta-analysis of liver function/inflammatory biomarkers; only TNF-alpha reached significance among many markers tested (ALT, AST, CRP, IL-6 all null), a weak and narrow finding relative to the selected cardio-metabolic meta-analyses.
Lipid-profile meta-analysis largely overlapping with the broader cardio-metabolic meta-analysis already selected (34981487); redundant for triage purposes.
CRP-only meta-analysis with a very small absolute effect size (WMD -0.017 mg/dL) driven mainly by non-healthy subjects; narrower and weaker than the selected sources.
Blood-pressure-only meta-analysis largely superseded by the more recent, methodologically similar dose-response meta-analysis already selected (39368321).
General narrative review of chlorogenic acid (a coffee compound, not green coffee bean extract specifically) across animal and human studies; not a focused GCBE efficacy analysis.

RCT of a 7-ingredient multi-component supplement (forskolin, green tea extract, beet root extract, alpha-lipoic acid, vitamin E, CoQ10, plus GCBE); effect cannot be attributed to green coffee bean extract alone.
RCT of green coffee bean extract combined with oat beta-glucans; a combination product, not single-ingredient GCBE evidence.
Small pilot RCT (n=16) on arterial stiffness (CAVI); underpowered and narrower than the selected larger meta-analyses and RCT.
